stem:
Kabir lines up four samples: ice cubes in a tray, water poured into a bottle, cooking oil poured into a bottle, and white mist above a boiling kettle.

Which of these are behaving as liquids? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Ice cubes in a tray that keep a fixed shape.
Water poured into a bottle, taking the shape of the bottle and able to flow.
Cooking oil poured into a bottle, taking the shape of the bottle and able to flow.
The white mist above a boiling kettle, treated as liquid because it can be seen.

teacher.key_rationale: A liquid flows and takes the container's shape. Water and oil do that. Ice keeps a fixed shape. Visible mist is not a liquid sample in a container.
